transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

Most often this is the hob protecting itself from overheating: restricted ventilation beneath it, a cooling fan that is not doing its job, or heat build-up from a large pan/high setting. A pan with a warped or unsuitable base can also make one zone behave oddly; less commonly it is the temperature sensor or control electronics. When it cuts out, does the whole hob switch off or only one cooking zone, and is any error letter/number shown? If it is set above an oven, avoid running the oven at the same time for one test and make sure any ventilation slots around/below the hob are not blocked; switch the hob off and isolate it before inspecting underneath.
just 1 zone, mostly the big front ones on high. a small code flashes but i didnt catch it. started after a new drawer unit was fitted under it last month

The timing after the drawer was fitted makes restricted cooling airflow the most likely cause. The larger front zones create the most heat, so they can reach the hob’s thermal cut-out first; it then stops that zone until it cools. With the hob switched off and isolated, check that the drawer or anything stored in it is not close to or blocking the hob underside/any ventilation space—don’t remove hob panels. The drawer installer may need to check the clearance against the hob manufacturer’s installation requirements. Also try the same zone with a different, flat induction pan that works well elsewhere, and get a photo of the flashing code if possible: that will separate a pan-detection issue from a cooling or zone-sensor fault. If the drawer clearance is correct and it still cuts out with a known-good pan, it is likely to need an engineer to investigate the cooling fan, temperature sensor or power module.
not removing the drawer or going under the hob, not doing that. fan roars before it cuts out tho. so is it the drawer or does it need an engineer?

On the evidence, the drawer installation is the first thing to investigate, not a failed fan: a roaring fan means it is at least attempting to cool the hob, and the problem began after the unit was fitted. One large front zone cutting out after several minutes on high fits thermal protection operating because heat cannot escape adequately beneath the hob. You do not need to take the drawer out yourself. Ask the drawer/kitchen installer to check the hob’s required underside ventilation and clearance against its installation instructions, including whether the drawer back, top, contents or any added panel has closed off the airflow. If they confirm the clearances are correct, then book an appliance engineer: the next likely causes are the affected zone’s temperature sensor or its power electronics. The fan running is normal; cutting out repeatedly is not.

candidates: Overheating protection due to restricted ventilation or cooling fan problem (high)
Pan/base compatibility or pan overheating causing the zone to reduce or stop (medium)
